answer: Hypothesis (data-grounded, observational): Using baseline 1985 composite wealth as a proxy for income level — because the dataset contains no income, earnings, or income-level variable — incarceration is associated with lower wealth among Black respondents (NLSY79; n=3,013; 159 jailed 1985–1994) in every baseline-wealth stratum, and the wealth differential is concentrated in the HIGH baseline-wealth stratum, not the low one. Concretely: among Black respondents in the top 1985-wealth tertile (median baseline wealth $11,875), the jailed had 1996 median wealth of $4,700 vs $26,750 for the non-jailed (median differential −$22,050; winsorized mean differential −$59,928), and a 1996-minus-1985 change of −$5,800 vs +$8,825 (−$14,625). In the middle tertile the 1996 median differential was −$7,450 (winsorized −$28,006). In the low tertile — which is essentially a zero-wealth group (median 1985 wealth $0; median 1996 wealth $0 for both groups) — the median differential was $0 and the gap is visible only in winsorized means (1996: −$13,878). Overall (unstratified), jailed Black respondents' median 1996 wealth was $0 vs $5,000 (−$5,000; Mann–Whitney p≈3e-12; winsorized mean differential −$32,097); restricting to Black males (n=1,465; 143 jailed) the pattern held (1996: $0 vs $5,450, p≈9e-11). Thus, to the extent 1985 wealth proxies income level, the incarceration–lower-wealth association is present across the distribution but largest among Black individuals with the highest baseline wealth/income proxy. This is an association, not a causal effect: no randomization, confounders (age, education, employment) are absent, and the 1985–1994 incarceration window overlaps the 1985 wealth measurement, so 1985 wealth is a concurrent, not strict pre-incarceration, baseline.

payload.workflow: Filtered to Black respondents (n=3,013; 159 jailed 1985–1994); stratified by tertiles of baseline composite_wealth_1985 (cutpoints 0 / 3,830) as the income-level proxy; within each stratum compared jailed vs non-jailed on 1990 and 1996 composite wealth and on change in wealth (1990−1985, 1996−1985) using medians, Mann–Whitney rank tests, and 1%–99% winsorized mean differentials; reported unstratified overall results and a Black-male sensitivity check; verified all strata had ≥30 jailed observations.
